{{nihongo|'''Hirose Shrine (Izunokuni)'''|広瀬神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Hirose Shrine''' (ひろせじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Takyo, {{ill|Izunokuni|ar|إزونوكني (شيزوكا)|arz|ازونوكنى|azb|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|ce|Идзунокуни|ceb|Izunokuni (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Izunokuni|es|Izunokuni (Shizuoka)|et|Izunokuni|fa|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|fi|Izunokuni|fr|Izunokuni|gl|Izunokuni|id|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|it|Izunokuni|ja|伊豆の国市|ko|이즈노쿠니시|mzn|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|nl|Izunokuni|pl|Izunokuni|pt|Izunokuni|ro|Izunokuni|ru|Идзунокуни|sv|Izunokuni|tg|Изунокуни|tl|Izunokuni|tr|İzunokuni|tt|Идзунокуни|tum|Izunokuni|uk|Ідзунокуні|vi|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|war|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|zh|伊豆之國市|zh_classical|伊豆之國市|zh_min_nan|Izunokuni-chhī|zh_yue|伊豆之國|qid=Q863758}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}.

=== History ===
According to a 1596 ridgepole inscription, it was moved during Tenpyō years (729-749) from Fukuda-no-shō in {{ill|Iyo Province|Q907829|qid=Q907829}}<ref>'Tōshū Shikō,' section on Fukuzawa Myōjin</ref>. The 'National Comprehensive Survey of Shrine Rites and Festivals' gives 733 as the founding year.

It is identified with the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (small) "Hirose Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}<ref name="散歩">Shizuoka Prefecture Japanese History Education Research Group (ed.), 'Historical Walks of Shizuoka Prefecture (Historical Walk 22),' Yamakawa Publishing, 2006, p.59</ref>.

It burned in military fire during the {{ill|Siege of Odawara (1590)|Q2622890|qid=Q2622890|lt=Odawara campaign}} of 1590, but was rebuilt in 1596.

Its enshrined deity {{ill|Tamakushi-hime|Q11572681|qid=Q11572681|lt=Shimomizo-ki-hime}} is the consort of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}, deity of {{ill|Mishima Taisha|el|Μισίμα Τάισα|fr|Mishima-taisha|ja|三嶋大社|tr|Mishima Tapınağı|zh|三嶋大社|qid=Q650772}}. It is said to have been temporarily enshrined here during Mishima Taisha's later transfer, and the two shrines remain closely connected.

Every year on November 3 an annual grand festival is held, where {{ill|Sanbasō|Q11356796|qid=Q11356796}} is performed<ref name="散歩"/><ref>[https://www.city.izunokuni.shizuoka.jp/tosikei/documents/2-7nirayama-oohito.pdf Historical character seen in shrine festivals and Sanbasō in Nirayama/Ōhito area] - Izunokuni City Urban Planning Division</ref>, and six {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} from local districts are operated. Float operation was canceled in {{ill|2020|Q25337|qid=Q25337}} (Reiwa 2) due to the spread of COVID-19. It resumed in {{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} (Reiwa 5), but due to lack of experience one float overturned, causing an accident with 19 dead or injured<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20231103-Z4WCFJ6QX5NOHFVRYUZCAKBYKI/ |title="Could not stop" festival float overturns, 1 dead and 18 injured |publisher=Sankei Shimbun |date=2023-11-03 |accessdate=2023-11-13}}</ref>.

In the {{ill|keidai|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002}} stands a poem monument of local {{ill|Waka poet|Q11122954|qid=Q11122954}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hozumi Tadashi}}. Tadashi was a disciple of {{ill|Shinobu Orikuchi|Q3482286|qid=Q3482286}} and {{ill|Hakushū Kitahara|Q1066026|qid=Q1066026}}<ref name="散歩"></ref>. His son is actor {{ill|Takanobu Hozumi|Q3546305|qid=Q3546305}}.
